title: Early Voting in Texas Starts Strong, With Democrats Turning Out in Larger Numbers
summaryZh: 德州提前投票兩天近150萬人投票，民主黨傾向選民比2024年更踴躍。
summaryHi: टेक्सस में शुरुआती दो दिनों में करीब 15 लाख वोट, डेमोक्रेट समर्थक ज़्यादा सक्रिय।
summaryEs: Casi 1,5 millones votan en Texas en dos días; el voto demócrata crece frente a 2024.
summaryJa: テキサス州の期日前投票、2日間で約150万人。民主党寄りの投票が増加。
summaryKo: 텍사스 사전투표 이틀간 약 150만 명 참여, 민주당 성향 투표 증가.
summaryEn: Nearly 1.5 million Texans voted early in two days, with Democrats doing better than in 2024.
paragraphs: Almost 1.5 million Texans cast their ballots in the first two days of early voting, and the early electorate looks noticeably more Democratic than it did in 2024, according to VoteHub, a data group working with the CBS News Data Desk.

Zachary Donnini, VoteHub's head of data science, said Monday's voters were about 10 points more Democratic than those on the first day of in-person early voting two years ago. Tuesday was slightly better for Republicans, at around eight or nine points more Democratic than the same day in 2024.

Because Texans do not register by party, analysts estimate party support from primary voting history. VoteHub calculates that 32% of people who have voted in Democratic primaries have already cast ballots, compared with nearly 21% of Republican primary voters. Donnini warned, however, that it is too early to draw conclusions.

The numbers matter because several races look close in a state that Donald Trump won by 14 points. A CBS News poll gives Democrat James Talarico 51% against Republican Ken Paxton's 49% in the Senate race, while Governor Greg Abbott leads Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 52% to 48%.
VoteHub expects two-thirds of Texas voters to vote early, and total turnout could come close to the 2024 presidential election. Nine days of early voting remain.
In Texas, people can vote early for the big election on 3 November. Early voting started on Monday.
In the first two days, almost 1.5 million people in Texas voted. That is a lot of people.
A data group called VoteHub looked at the voters. It says more Democrats voted in these two days than in 2024. But it also says it is too early to know who will win.
Two big races are close. For the Senate, Democrat James Talarico is a little ahead of Republican Ken Paxton. For governor, Republican Greg Abbott is a little ahead of Democrat Gina Hinojosa.
Early voting will go on for nine more days. Both parties want their people to vote soon.
Nearly 1.5 million people in Texas voted in the first two days of early voting for the November elections, according to the data group VoteHub, which works with CBS News.

VoteHub's head of data science, Zachary Donnini, said the people who voted on Monday were about 10 points more Democratic than on the first day of early voting in 2024. On Tuesday, the difference was a little smaller, about eight or nine points.

In Texas, voters do not register with a party, so the group looked at who voted in past party primaries. About 32% of people who usually vote in Democratic primaries have already voted, compared with almost 21% of Republican primary voters. Still, Donnini said it was too early to make conclusions.

The races are important. Donald Trump won Texas by 14 points in 2024, but polls show Democrat James Talarico slightly ahead of Republican Ken Paxton in the Senate race. Republican Governor Greg Abbott leads Democrat Gina Hinojosa by a small amount.
VoteHub expects two out of three Texans to vote early this year. There are nine days of early voting left.

Donnini warned, however, that it is too early to draw conclusions.

Nearly 1.5 million Texans voted in the opening two days of early voting, and the initial electorate is tilting more Democratic than it did in 2024, according to an analysis by VoteHub, which partners with the CBS News Data Desk.

Zachary Donnini, the group's head of data science, said Monday's voters were roughly 10 points more Democratic than on the first day of in-person early voting two years earlier, although Tuesday proved somewhat kinder to Republicans, with the gap narrowing to eight or nine points.

Since Texas has no party registration, partisan turnout has to be inferred from primary voting records. By VoteHub's estimate, 32% of people with a history of voting in Democratic primaries have already cast ballots, against just under 21% of Republican primary voters. Donnini nonetheless cautioned that it is far too early to draw conclusions, stressing that a strong poll lead does not automatically translate into victory.

The stakes are high in a state Donald Trump carried by 14 points. Democrat James Talarico holds a narrow edge over Republican Ken Paxton in the Senate contest, while Governor Greg Abbott retains a slim lead over Democrat Gina Hinojosa.
With nine days of early voting still to go, VoteHub projects that two-thirds of Texans will vote early.

Early voting figures from Texas suggest unusually strong participation among Democratic-leaning voters, although analysts caution against reading too much into the first two days, during which almost 1.5 million ballots were cast.

According to VoteHub, a data organisation collaborating with CBS News, Monday's electorate was approximately 10 points more Democratic than on the corresponding day in 2024, while Tuesday's was eight or nine points more Democratic. Since Texans do not register by party, these estimates are based on voters' previous participation in party primaries: around 32% of Democratic primary voters have already voted, compared with roughly 21% of their Republican counterparts.

The significance of these figures lies in the competitiveness of several contests. Although Donald Trump won the state by 14 points in 2024, Democrat James Talarico narrowly leads Republican Ken Paxton in polls for the Senate, while Governor Greg Abbott maintains a modest advantage over his challenger, Gina Hinojosa.

Nevertheless, VoteHub's head of data science, Zachary Donnini, emphasised that turnout does not automatically translate into victory, and that Democratic candidates would also need to persuade some Trump voters.
With nine days of early voting remaining, overall turnout is projected to approach the level of the last presidential election.
